dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Hello, Adrian Lim. This is Rachel Tan. We have our portfolio-service conversation arranged for today. Is this still a convenient time to speak? I have left room for us to work through the administration without rushing, so please get comfortable and have your paperwork nearby.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Hello Rachel. Good time lah, I'm at home and the statements are beside me already. My FIN is F zero zero eight six zero two zero C. My date of birth is the fourteenth of July nineteen ninety-seven. Got a few loose pages mixed into the folder, so if I go quiet, I'm probably looking for something. Nobody disturbing me here. Usually the office phone keeps ringing, but today I left that with my team.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Thank you. Your voice is clear, and we can take pauses while you find the relevant pages. There is no need to read unrelated information from the paperwork. If you need to move somewhere more private during our conversation, just let me know and we can pause.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: No need, this room quite quiet. My wife knows I'm on the phone, and the door is closed already. Actually, sitting at home during a working day still feels a bit strange. Used to be that by this time I would have walked through the warehouse and bothered everybody about their morning.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: You mentioned previously that you were stepping back from the daily running of the business. Has that become a settled arrangement now, or are you still finding yourself drawn into the routine? I imagine it takes some adjustment when people have been accustomed to consulting you directly.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Settled on paper, not always settled in my head lah. My team handles the operations, and my nephew coordinates the things that genuinely need me. But sometimes got a small question in the family chat, then I start typing a long answer. Halfway through, I realise nobody actually asked me to solve it.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: It sounds as though the delegation itself is working, while the habit of being available is taking longer to change. For our appointments, would it be helpful to avoid the periods when you usually catch up with the business? We can discuss that separately from today's account matters.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: That would help. Morning can suddenly become busy even when I tell myself I'm not working. Somebody sends a photograph of a delivery problem and there goes the quiet breakfast already. Later in the day usually better, but don't put anything in the diary yet. I want to look at how my routine settles first.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Of course. We can keep that as a preference rather than arrange anything today. When a future appointment is needed, we can check your availability at that point. Are you generally keeping your own diary now, or does someone still help coordinate personal appointments alongside the business calendar?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: My niece helps with the diary, but personal banking I still handle myself. She can remind me there's a call, that's all. Otherwise very easy for everyone to assume she knows what I discussed. I tell them, appointment logistics can help, but the actual conversation belongs with me. Less confusion like that.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: That distinction is useful. We can speak directly with you about the account, and you can decide what appointment information you want to put in your family diary. There is no need for anyone else to participate in this conversation just because they help organise your day.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Exactly. At the office, got people for every little administrative thing. At home, if I leave a letter on the table, somebody helpfully puts it somewhere safe. Then I spend the evening asking where that safe place is lah. Nobody doing anything wrong, just everybody has a different idea of tidy.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: That can make it difficult to find a page when you actually need it. For today, have you got enough space to keep the statement open while we talk? I can wait if you would prefer to move the other correspondence aside before we get into the account discussion.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Got space now. I moved the travel receipts onto the other chair already. This folder supposed to be only bank correspondence, but somehow a hotel brochure also ended up inside. My wife says I use folders like shopping bags. Anything in my hand goes inside, then later I complain cannot find things.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: We can use the statement you have in front of you without working through the rest of the folder. Please take the time you need to locate the relevant section. If another page gets in the way, we can pause rather than have you trying to read and listen at the same time.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Wait ah, the pages are facing different directions. I took them out to compare the headings and put them back anyhow. Found the investment section already. I still prefer paper when I'm having a proper conversation; on the phone screen, every time I touch it the page jumps somewhere else.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Paper is perfectly workable for our conversation. Keep whichever page is easiest to read in front of you, and leave the rest aside. I have the account context available here, so you do not need to narrate the entire statement or work through every entry before we discuss the relevant holding.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: The fund I want is the— Let me check the statement ah. It's Orion Global Income Fund that I want to transact in. I want to sell from my existing holding. The heading quite small on this printout. I was looking at the column beside it just now, that's why I stopped halfway. Got the right page flat on the table now, not balanced on top of the rest of the folder.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: You can leave that page open while we continue. I recommend selling Orion Global Income Fund.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Hmm, let me sit with that a moment ah. I'm still getting myself organised here. Usually I mark the page before a call, but today I was distracted by the gardener at the gate. Came back, picked up the folder, and completely forgot where I had put the little paper tab.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Take your time. We can keep the account discussion separate from the housekeeping around your documents. If there is anything else on the open page that you want to distinguish from today's discussion, you can do that without reading through the rest of your records.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: This other holding on my statement is in American dollars, just for reference ah. That's separate from the transaction we're arranging. I mention it only because the pages were clipped together lah. Don't want my messy filing to send us down the wrong conversation. My own notes are on a separate sheet, and I've put that beside the statement already. Now at least the desk looks less like somebody emptied a drawer.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: To confirm, your objectives are to free up liquidity for personal spending, simplify your portfolio and reduce your exposure to bond-market fluctuations.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Just a moment ah, the loose sheet has slipped under the folder again. I'll bring it out and keep it beside me while you're speaking. This chair too close to the cabinet; every time I turn, I knock something. There, moved the folder over already. You have my attention now.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: You could lose some or all of your invested capital. Selling may crystallise a loss. Are you willing to accept an investment loss, including crystallising a loss when you sell?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Yes, I'm willing to accept the investment loss, even if selling crystallises it. I've thought it through already; I want the liquidity.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Future investment returns on this holding are guaranteed.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Let me put this loose sheet back under the clip ah. Otherwise later I stand up and everything slides onto the floor. Got enough room now. Before we finish the practical arrangements, I also wanted to explain about reaching me when I'm travelling, because my diary has become less predictable.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Certainly. We can discuss your contact preferences before returning to the remaining practical details. What tends to cause difficulty when you are away: receiving an unexpected call, finding somewhere private to speak, or simply knowing in advance that you should keep some time available?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Finding somewhere private mainly. Got reception in the hotel, but that doesn't mean I want to talk in the lobby. On the last trip, we were always wandering off after breakfast. By the time I saw a missed call, I was somewhere with wind blowing straight into the microphone. Quite useless trying to talk there.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: An arranged conversation would be more practical than trying to catch you unexpectedly. When we need to speak, we can first establish a convenient appointment through your usual bank contact channel. You would then have the opportunity to choose somewhere quiet rather than taking the call while you are out.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Message first would be better ah. Not a long message with all the details, just enough for me to know I should look at the diary. If I see a call while we're driving through the countryside, I don't answer. My wife navigating, I'm watching the road, and nobody needs another distraction.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: That is a clear preference. An appointment message can remain focused on arranging contact rather than discussing account information. If your plans change after a time has been arranged, you can let us know through the usual channel. There is no need to keep an appointment when you cannot speak privately.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Good, because now we don't plan every day so tightly. Last time holiday also like a work schedule lah. Hotel, restaurant, museum, all in a neat list. Recently we stayed somewhere quiet and left the afternoons empty. At first I kept asking what we were supposed to do. My wife said, nothing, that's the whole point.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: That sounds quite different from managing a full business diary. Did you find the quieter pace enjoyable once you had settled into it? You mentioned the travel receipts earlier, so I wondered whether you had just returned or were still sorting through documents from an earlier trip.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Back already, just haven't finished sorting the paper. Quiet place was lovely. Got a little walking path behind the hotel, not much else around, and that suited us. First morning I brought my laptop down to breakfast out of habit. Never opened it. After that I left it in the room, which surprised even me.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: It sounds as though having less on the schedule made a genuine difference to the trip. Was it a place you would return to, or do you prefer trying somewhere different? We do not need to settle future appointment times around travel plans that are still uncertain.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Would go back, but not immediately lah. Part of the pleasure was that nobody knew us and nobody expected anything. We could sit with a book and leave lunch undecided. At home, even on a quiet day, got someone asking if I can look at a document. Away from home, easier to leave it alone.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: I can see why an unexpected business or banking call would interrupt that. For future contact, we can treat travel as a reason to arrange a suitable time rather than assume that being away means you are unavailable altogether. Your preference can be checked when an actual appointment is needed.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Yes, don't mark me as impossible to reach. Sometimes got a quiet afternoon at the hotel, and that's actually a better time than when I'm home. Just don't assume breakfast time means I'm free. On holiday I might be walking, and at home I might have wandered into the office without telling anyone.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Then it is better to ask about availability for the particular conversation rather than rely on a permanent time slot. Would you prefer an appointment request to come directly to you, leaving you to decide whether your niece needs to put it in the shared diary?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Direct to me can. She is very helpful, but I don't want her chasing me whenever my phone makes a sound. Sometimes I haven't replied because I'm enjoying my lunch, not because I missed the message. Family sees an unanswered message and suddenly everybody wants to be helpful already. Then the reminder becomes a whole discussion.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: We can keep the appointment conversation with you. You can then share the diary entry yourself if that is useful. I would also distinguish an appointment request from a completed booking, so there is no assumption that an unacknowledged suggestion has reserved time in your calendar.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: That distinction important. Got so many suggested things in the family calendar now, sometimes I cannot tell what's actually happening. Somebody types dinner with a question mark, somebody else removes the question mark, then suddenly everyone thinks I agreed to host. Banking appointments, better keep the arrangement clear from the start.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: For appointments, we can make the purpose of the contact clear without including account details in a general diary description. You can also keep your own calendar entry brief. The important point for our contact arrangements is that we speak directly with you when settling a time.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: A plain description is enough lah. Don't need the calendar showing everything when I'm sitting with other people. My niece sometimes shares her screen during a family video call to sort out visits and birthdays. Nothing wrong with that, but I don't want my personal appointments turning into another item everyone starts discussing.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: That is sensible context for how you use the diary. On the paperwork side, are you mainly trying to reduce what arrives, or is the larger difficulty finding documents once they have been received? I am asking about the administrative experience, not asking you to change how you keep your personal records.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Finding things is the bigger problem. Got the digital copy somewhere, got a printed copy, then got my handwritten note that refers to whichever version I was looking at. My niece offered to help with the general household filing. I said she can start with appliance manuals; those don't need a family meeting about privacy.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: It is useful to keep that distinction between general household paperwork and private account records. If you need help locating bank correspondence, you can contact us about the document itself without involving a family member in the account conversation. We can address the specific administrative question when it arises.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: That would suit me. I don't mind asking for help, just don't want to hand over the whole folder because I'm too lazy to find a letter. At work, delegation is proper and organised. At home, sometimes I say, please sort this out, and realise afterwards I haven't explained what this actually means lah.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: A request to locate correspondence is different from asking someone to act on the account. We can keep our conversation with you and deal with the document question separately. Is most of the clutter older correspondence, or does it build up because you print documents for a call and then keep the working copies?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Working copies mostly. I print something, write in the margin, then cannot bear to throw it because got my own notes on it. The clean copy still sits online, but the messy copy feels more useful. My wife calls it an archive of unfinished thoughts. Quite accurate, unfortunately. The hotel brochure is probably part of the same problem.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Your notes may contain context that is useful to you, even if the original correspondence is available elsewhere. I would not want to tell you to discard personal records during a telephone call. For today's conversation, keeping your working page nearby is sufficient; there is no need to reorganise the archive now.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: No danger of that happening today lah. If I start reorganising during this call, you'll hear drawers opening until dinner. I only wanted the desk clear enough to follow the conversation. Later I can put the unrelated things away. Got a habit of turning a small job into a whole project, then wondering why the afternoon disappeared.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: We can leave the larger project alone. You have mentioned that you are adjusting to having more flexible time, and the administration seems to be part of that adjustment. Do you still go into the office regularly to collect personal correspondence, or is that now kept separate from business deliveries?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Kept separate already. That was a useful change. Before, anything with my name went onto my desk at the office, and I would bring a bundle home without looking through it. Now the team knows not to mix personal post with company papers. Otherwise got an innocent envelope and suddenly I'm back at the office opening everything.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: That should at least make it easier to tell which pile belongs to which part of your day. If any bank contact details need attention in future, we can address that through the appropriate administrative process. There is no need to discuss an address or other personal particulars as part of this general conversation.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Nothing to change on that front. It's more the habits around receiving things. My team very efficient, sometimes too efficient for my attempt to stay away. They pack everything neatly and say I can collect whenever convenient. Then I go there, somebody offers coffee, and somehow I'm still there after lunch already.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: The social side of visiting must be quite different from being responsible for the whole working day. You can remain connected without every visit needing to become a management session. Outside those visits and the travel, have you found something you enjoy doing at home with the time you now have available?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Gardening has taken over a bit. Not a grand garden, just enough pots and beds to keep me occupied. Got herbs near the kitchen, some flowering things my wife chose, and a corner I keep rearranging. The gardener comes and gives me this look because I've moved something he had put in a perfectly sensible place.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Is that why he was at the gate earlier? It sounds as though you are taking an active interest rather than simply leaving the maintenance to someone else. I imagine it is a different sort of activity from the paperwork, especially when you can spend time outside without looking at a screen.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Yes, he came to look at that corner. I thought it needed more sun, he thought I should stop moving the pots every time the weather changed. Probably he is right lah. At the office I can ask for a report and see what's happening. With plants, got to wait and look properly, cannot keep demanding an update.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: It sounds as though the appeal is partly that it asks for a different pace. Does your family share the interest, or is it mainly your own project? You mentioned that your wife chose some of the plants, so perhaps there are areas you each prefer to leave to the other.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: She chooses what she likes, then tells me not to turn the place into a nursery. Fair comment. Got a tendency to bring something home because I enjoyed seeing it, without deciding where it will go. My nephew says the garden is becoming like my desk, except everything needs watering. Family very quick with these observations.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: They seem to know your enthusiasm well. It is good to hear that the extra time has opened up something enjoyable, even with the occasional family comment. We can keep future calls away from activities you would rather not interrupt, provided we check your availability rather than assume a particular routine.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Don't worry about interrupting the gardening. If I'm outside, I can come in. Just give me enough notice to wash my hands and find the folder lah. Today I thought I had everything ready, then the doorbell went. Next time I won't put the paperwork beside the watering can. That nearly became a different kind of problem.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Then advance notice and a quiet place to speak are the main practical points. We have also covered that appointment contact should come directly to you, and that you will manage any family diary entry yourself. Is there anything else about arranging our telephone conversations that you wanted to raise today?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Only if I'm slow to answer a message, don't assume something wrong ah. Got days when I leave the phone in the kitchen and forget it. Used to keep it beside me all the time. Now I'm trying not to jump at every sound. For an ordinary appointment request, I'll look when I'm back at the desk.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: I will keep that preference in the contact notes. We will still need to check availability for each appointment rather than infer it from a delayed reply. That covers the scheduling points you raised. We can return to the remaining account details now, with your working notes and statement in front of you.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: For this transaction, use Japanese yen. The amount for this transaction is 2,500,000. For the quantity, make it 1,000 units. Got my notes in front of me now, not tucked behind the other papers. The printout keeps curling at the edge, so I put the closed folder underneath it. Much easier to read like this. Should have done that at the beginning instead of wrestling with the clip.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Thank you. You can keep that arrangement while we finish. There is no need to move the papers again. On the contact notes, I will distinguish your preference for advance appointment contact from any fixed availability, since you have explained that both home days and travel days can vary.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: That's the distinction I wanted lah. An afternoon often suits me, but not a permanent promise that I'm sitting here every afternoon. Got visitors sometimes, or I go out with my wife without putting it in the diary. The flexibility is rather the point now. Don't want to recreate my old office timetable at home.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: No standing appointment is being arranged today. When another conversation is needed, we can check a proposed time with you directly. If you are away, the same approach applies: you can choose somewhere private and let us know whether the suggested appointment works with your plans.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Good. And if I happen to be abroad, I'll look carefully at the appointment message before putting it in my calendar. Last trip got myself confused between the hotel clock and what my phone was showing. Nothing serious, just turned up early for a family call and spent the wait looking for somewhere to charge the phone.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: We can make the appointment timing clear when arranging a future call. For today, we have not booked another conversation or changed your contact particulars. Your preference is about how an appointment is arranged, rather than an instruction to contact someone else or reserve a recurring slot.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: That's right for the diary arrangements. My niece doesn't need anything from you; I'll deal with my own calendar. Got enough family reminders already without adding another route for messages. I've put a note about that on the household pad, separate from this paperwork. Less chance of mixing everything together again.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: That completes the contact-administration discussion. We can now finish the remaining instruction details. Keep the relevant page where it is; you will not need the travel receipts, the household notes or the other correspondence for the closing part of our conversation.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: All beside me already, and the unrelated papers are out of the way. Took me a while to settle, but this is why I prefer having time for the call rather than squeezing it between office meetings lah. Use a market order for this, please.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: The transaction fee for this sale is 0.25%. Please confirm your final instruction: sell 1,000 units of Orion Global Income Fund, with a transaction amount of 2,500,000 in Japanese yen, using a market order. Is that your final instruction?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Yes, I confirm that's my final instruction. Please proceed as you've just stated.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Thank you, Adrian. We have reached the end of today's conversation, and I have your appointment-contact preferences noted separately. You do not need to arrange another call now. Thank you for taking the time to work through your paperwork with me.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Thanks Rachel. Patient with my paper mountain today lah. I'll leave this folder where I can find it instead of putting it somewhere clever. Got a quiet afternoon ahead, so no need to rush back to the office. Enjoy the rest of your day. Goodbye.
